newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel short bonds end higher on new CPI worries.
newsitem.headline: Israel short bonds end higher on new CPI worries.

text.p: Inflation-indexed short bonds continued their rise on Monday, as the decline in the Israeli shekel against the dollar since last Wednesday sparked renewed concerns about inflation, traders said.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: +0.21 pct to 168.10
* CPI (consumer price index) linked government bonds: +0.2 pct to 168.62
* Dollar-linked government bonds: +0.27 pct at 168.26
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years): -0.01 pct to 167.1
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.05 pct at 158.45
"There was big demand, especially for long bonds," said Gila Shkury, an investment counseller at Israel Discount Bank. Turnover was relatively high at 157 million shekels.
For the second day, inflation-indexed short bonds joined the overall rise, with yields reaching 4.6 percent.

Short bonds have turned higher on renewed fears that inflation may not come down as quickly as originally expected since the shekel fell more than two percent against the dollar since last Wednesday, said Shkury. She said the weaker shekel would translate into higher inflation.
However, Shmuel Hoffert, head of trading at United Mizrahi Bank, said he continued to remain optimistic about inflation because the slowdown in the economy would help contain price rises.

Last week the bond market was encouraged by a low September CPI and reports that the government was preparing a wide-ranging economic programme including further budget cuts in 1997. As a result, the Bank of Israel is expected to reduce the base short-term rate next week by up to 0.5 percentage point from the current 15.5 percent.

Shkury said the relatively big gain in September money supply released on Sunday was not discouraging. "The increase in the means of payment was due to seasonal factors and won't influence interest rates," she said.
"If he (Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel) does cut interest rates, no one expects a big cut," she said.

Dollar-linked bonds were stable, with some moderate rise in dollar short bonds. That was in line with trends on the local foreign currency market on Monday, where the dollar represenative rate was set at 3.27 shekels.
"At the start there was a strengthening in the dollar, but later in the day it began falling, and the dollar closed at nearly the same price as in the morning," Hoffert said.
Unlinked bonds were also unchanged, with the Makam trading at yields of 15.7 percent.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1= 3.27 shekels)
- David Rosenberg, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211
